name: Bookstore Party: Treasure Hunt Edition with Mysticeti
description: Go on a treasure hunt. Make a zine. Connect with new stories.  Mysticeti Studio’s   ‘Bookstore Party’  celebrates the love for books in unexpected ways – a treasure hunt that unfolds through a zine.  Join us for the  ‘Bookstore Party’  where we invite you to re-discover your favourite bookstore while being on the “hunt” for new stories. This Party is for all ages and for book nerds to spend time among books and explore new corners. What to expect? Participate in a self-paced, gamified bookshop browsing experience. Find personalised clues hidden in the bookshop, spend time browsing different shelves to find answers, create zines inspired by the stories you discover, and create an outline for your own story. Here are the details: Date:  1 November 2026, Sunday Time:  11:00 AM - 12:30 PM Venue:  Champaca Bookstore, Vasanth Nagar Ages:   All ages. Children can be accompanied by an adult to participate together. Workshop fee:   INR 499/-  Limited seats.  Register here . Know your Facilitator: Stuti Sareen  is a creative educator and curator working across art, storytelling, and community engagement. She is the founder of Mysticeti Studio and Kauri Centre, where she designs learning programmes, creative experiences and independent publications. Her practice centres on creating accessible spaces for dialogue, experimentation, and artistic exchange. She lives in Goa and Varanasi. About Mysticeti: Mysticeti  is an independent publishing house, community centre, and creative programming initiative.  Register to reserve your spot.

name: Book Discussion | ‘A Moving Line’: Evolving Identities in Comics and Graphic Narratives
description: Join us for the book discussion of  A Moving Line , a celebration of India’s rich history of visual storytelling. Comic creator and visual artists  Rahil Mohsin  and  Mia Jose  will be in conversation with designer  Kriti Monga  to reflect on how storytelling in graphic narratives have evolved over centuries and the many nuances and developments in it.  This will be followed by an interactive Q&A with the audience. This conversation has been curated in collaboration with Museum of Art & Photography.   Here are the details: Date:  31st October 2026, Sunday Time:  6:00 PM (seating begins at 5:45 PM) Venue:  Champaca Bookstore, Vasanth Nagar RSVP here  to register. About the book:   Stories, whether written or drawn, are always moving, reshaped by every generation that inherits and retells them. India has a long and rich history of visual storytelling, from temple walls and painted scrolls to comics, graphic novels and webcomics. Published by the Museum of Art and Photography,  A Moving Line  traces this history, revealing unexpected connections between works that are rarely considered together. The eight essays and eleven graphic narratives in this collection range from the timeless to the future-forward. Bringing together contributions by scholars, practitioners and artists, this book explores the many nuances and developments in sequential storytelling. A Moving Line  celebrates a medium that has always been, and continues to be, inherently visual. Meet the speakers: Rahil Mohsin  is a Bangalore-based comic artist, writer, and co-founder of  Hallubol , the world’s first bilingual Dakhni-English comic series. With over 15 years in comics and illustration, he has worked with publishers, both international and local including Scout Comics, Scholastic, Sufi Comics and Comixense and is a familiar face in the thriving independent Indian comics scene. He has illustrated children’s books for Room to Read, while Pratham's  Fayu & Dariya Ka Jinn  marks his debut as both writer and illustrator. His work explores language, folklore, memory, food, and everyday life through comics and picture books. Rooted in his Dakhni Muslim identity and upbringing in Bangalore, his practice celebrates multilingual storytelling, cultural memory, neighbourhoods, and South Indian experiences.  Mia Shay Jose  (she/they) is a trans artist and researcher from Kerala, currently based in New Delhi. Led by a keen sense of narrative, her work probes questions of gender, inheritance and embodiment in cultural stories, informed by her lived experiences of transition: of body, culture and faith. She approaches systems both through the lens of a transgender body and that of a legal researcher, searching for a reconciliation of conflicted parts essential to the self. Over the last 2 years, this search has led to  Negotiations , a comic travelogue charting the policing of non-binary bodies across public spaces,  Regards Your Skin , an anthology around self-policing and motherhood, and a public mural with trans communities in Kerala. Her primary interest is in the physical body as the primary site of violence - inflicted both by a deeply binary society, and as a consequence, the self. Across illustrations, writings, collage, installations and comics, her works are grounded in the dialogue between constructed identities and policed spaces. Meet the moderator: Kriti Monga  brings over two decades of design experience to her multi-disciplinary practice, blending artistic expression, strategic design, and hands-on craftsmanship. The founder-director of the acclaimed Turmeric Design, her work spans brand building, book design, visual art, illustration, and mentorship. She also teaches professional design and typography programs globally. RSVP to reserve your spot.
